source.title: FastFill: Efficient Compatible Model Update
source.authors: Florian Jaeckle; Fartash Faghri; Ali Farhadi; O. Tuzel; H. Pouransari

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a learned transformation can make old and new model features compatible for retrieval, using retrieval performance rather than a direct comparison of representation-distance geometries.
record.gate_note: The paper studies image-embedding compatibility during model updates, not whether representations converge as model scale or capability increases. It reports retrieval and backfilling results for learned feature maps. Results cited from prior work are not included as rows. Figure-only backfilling curves are described but not separately transcribed where the tables provide numeric summaries or ablations.
record.test_reason: The independently trained FCT/FastFill embedding models are evaluated using learned old-to-new feature maps, which bears on V4. However, most recorded values average retrieval over partial backfilling and cannot establish how little performance is lost through mapping alone. Compatibility-constrained BCT/RACT training does not test interchangeability of independently learned representations.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct: FastFill combines learned feature alignment and uncertainty-based partial backfilling to improve retrieval during model updates, including an architecture change, and reduces a gender accuracy gap with limited backfilling. Qualify the compatibility statement: Section 4.2 explicitly describes incomplete compatibility of previous methods; the paper does not establish a uniform mapping-loss result across all FastFill settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a learned MLP transformation from old to new image-feature space, retrieval evaluation, and partial backfilling; it does not directly measure representational distance similarity or scale-driven convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with dataset, old/new architecture, alignment loss, backfilling order, and availability of side-information. The paper reports that uncertainty-based ordering improves results over random ordering and that the combined alignment loss outperforms some loss ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: BCT/RACT backfilling comparisons evaluate systems explicitly trained for compatibility.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compatibility-specific model training can improve retrieval during model updates.

fits_no_version.finding: FastFill improves average retrieval during backfilling through its alignment objective and uncertainty-based ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned update policy can reduce the amount of image recomputation needed to improve retrieval.

record.problems: The outcome is downstream retrieval performance rather than a direct measure of representation-distance alignment. No uncertainty intervals or statistical tests are reported despite averaging five runs. Several additional backfilling curves are figure-based. The paper does not report a numeric new-model single-model reference alongside the main average-backfilling tables.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted under the 60-row cap. Additional figure-only backfilling curves, CMC-top5 summary comparisons, further ImageNet/Places/VGGFace2 ablations (including Tables 6-7 and Figures 8-12), and the biased-model gender-gap results are not separately rowed here; they concern ordering, task accuracy, or further variants rather than direct representational geometry.

untested.parts: No convergence-versus-scale or capability analysis across independently trained models.
Repeated random seeds are experimental repetitions, not measurements of shared features or subspaces across seeds.

No linear-map comparison, stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or general downstream interchangeability test. Maps are trained with paired old/new features, and FastFill also uses labels and the new classifier.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits.
No comparison of representation-similarity metrics or their settings. Retrieval metrics and ordering policies do not establish this version.
No convergence plateau analysis or causal test of shared training data/objectives as explanations.

missing.what: A qualitative zero-versus-full-backfilling result: VGGFace2 transformations already achieve high compatibility, with a relatively small remaining retrieval gap. Record this separately from backfilling averages.
A qualitative mapping-objective result: discriminative-only alignment, with or without uncertainty, gives poor compatibility at zero backfilling. The existing ablation rows record averages instead.

record.verdict_notes: Absolute retrieval accuracy is not the fraction of representation interchangeability preserved. Backfilling averages mix transformed old features with newly computed features, so their numerical values do not justify the record's blanket partial states or its single limits_scope verdict. The explicitly declared omitted curves and further ablations are not added as missing results.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep and no test of convergence across independently trained models with varied architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language model comparison.
No comparison of features or subspaces learned from different random seeds of the same architecture.

Tests learned old-to-new feature transformations for image retrieval, including an MLP map and a changed-architecture setting. Does not test linear maps, stitching, relative representations, unpaired-data mappings, or preservation of representation geometry directly.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.
Does not compare representation-similarity measures, neighbour counts, or in- versus out-of-distribution geometry.
Does not test whether shared data or objectives explain representational convergence or whether convergence plateaus.

relationships.condition: VGGFace2, learned feature transformation before backfilling
relationships.reason: Based on Section 5.2 rather than the averaged rows: the authors explicitly report high compatibility and a small gap between zero and full backfilling.
relationships.display_finding: The authors reported high compatibility and a small performance gap between zero and full backfilling.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-1k, discriminative-only alignment map, with or without uncertainty
relationships.reason: Based on Appendix C.1 rather than the averaged rows: these maps have poor compatibility at zero backfilling, showing dependence on the mapping objective.
relationships.display_finding: Discriminative-only maps had poor compatibility at zero backfilling, whether or not uncertainty was included.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet-1k, VGGFace2, Places-365, architecture-change, ablation, and side-information experiments
reader_labels.reason: Learned transformations yield useful cross-model retrieval and FastFill outperforms several alternatives, but the paper says compatibility remains incomplete: cross-model retrieval is significantly worse than single-model retrieval, and partial backfilling is needed to close that gap. See r1-r52.
